facts.claim: Sherpas and Tibetans call Everest Chomolungma, most often put as 'Goddess Mother of the World'; Sherpa mothers told their children it meant the mountain so high that no bird can fly over it.

versions.note: Chomolungma means 'Goddess Mother of the World' or 'Goddess of the Valley'.

source.title: Britannica: What are other names for Mount Everest?

versions.note: Also put as 'Goddess Mother of the Wind'; Sherpa mothers told their children it meant 'the mountain so high that no bird can fly over it'.

source.title: Michael Ward: The Name of the World's Highest Peak (The Himalayan Journal 53)

facts.claim: Sherpas believe the goddess Miyolangsangma lives on Everest's summit, a goddess of inexhaustible giving who wants respect and offerings, and that a climber must win her favour before going up.

versions.note: The Tibetan Buddhist goddess who lives at the top of Chomolungma, one of the five long-life sisters; her virtue is inexhaustible giving.
Sherpas believe climbers must appease her first to reach the summit safely; her generosity asks to be met with respect and offerings.

source.title: Tsem Rinpoche: Miyolangsangma, the Goddess of Inexhaustible Giving

facts.claim: Before a team climbs, a lama holds a puja at Base Camp: he asks the mountain's gods to let the climbers pass, to forgive them for hurting the mountain with their sharp points, and to keep them safe; the crampons and the axes are brought to be blessed. Nobody goes up the Icefall before it.

versions.note: A lama from a local village prays to the mountain gods before any serious climbing, asking forgiveness for hurting the mountains with sharp points; harnesses, crampons and ice axes are brought to it.

source.title: Alan Arnette: Everest 2021: Puja Before Climbing

versions.note: A must-do before anyone enters the Icefall; for the Sherpas, an homage to Miyolangsangma, who lives on the summit; barley flour smeared on each other for a white beard and a long life.

source.title: Alan Arnette: Everest 2024: Tibet Climbs in Peril

facts.claim: Each time before they leave Base Camp for the Icefall, the climbers and the Sherpas pass by the puja's altar and let the smoke of burning juniper cover them.

versions.note: Every time before leaving Base Camp, each climber and Sherpa passes the spot, letting the smoke from the juniper boughs cover them.

source.title: Alan Arnette: Everest 2021: Puja Before Climbing

facts.claim: Many Sherpas are named for the day of the week they were born on: Dawa Monday, Mingma Tuesday, Lhakpa Wednesday, Phurba Thursday, Pasang Friday, Pemba Saturday, Nyima Sunday.

versions.note: Pemba: born on a Saturday; the article lists all seven days.

source.title: B. R. Goodfellow: Suggested Explanations of Sherpa Names (The Himalayan Journal 20, 1957)

facts.claim: On the summit, Tenzing Norgay called out 'Thuji chey, Chomolungma': thank you, Chomolungma.

versions.note: When Tenzing Norgay Sherpa summited, he called out 'Thuji chey, Chomolungma'.

source.title: Alan Arnette: What's in a name: Everest, Chomolungma, Sagarmatha? (2020)

facts.claim: A Sherpa takes a bad dream before a climb as a sign: in 2021 Kami Rita Sherpa turned back from Camp 3 on his 26th attempt, the weather turning and the goddess, he said, telling him in a dream it was enough.

versions.note: 'I didn't have a good dream. I felt the goddess was telling me it is enough for this time.' Sherpas consider the peak holy.

source.title: The Himalayan Times (Reuters): Record-breaking Sherpa says mountain goddess warned him from 26th Everest ascent

versions.note: Sherpas believe Everest to be a goddess and hold a religious ceremony before stepping on the mountain.

source.title: AP via NewsChannel 9: Bad dream stops Mount Everest guide from climbing peak for the 26th time

facts.claim: How many times a climbing Sherpa goes through the Khumbu Icefall in a season, carrying the expedition's loads.

versions.note: Sherpa trips through the icefall can be as many as 30 to 40 a season.

source.title: National Geographic: Nepalis Hold Their Breath as New Everest Climbing Season Begins (2016)

versions.note: Not uncommon for Sherpas to go through the Khumbu Icefall around 30 times each season.

facts.claim: How many times a paying client goes through the Khumbu Icefall in a season: three or four round trips.

versions.note: A regular paying client might make six to eight trips.

source.title: National Geographic: Nepalis Hold Their Breath as New Everest Climbing Season Begins (2016)

versions.note: The average client passes through the Khumbu six to eight times, three or four round trips; the average Sherpa ten times that.

source.title: National Geographic: The new climbing season begins with a 'safer' route through a killer icefall (2015)

facts.claim: Words a guide in the Khumbu uses with clients on the trail: bistari, bistari, Nepali for 'slowly, slowly', and jam jam, 'let's go'.

versions.note: Bistari bistari, 'slowly, slowly', the most important phrase on the trail; jam jam, 'let's go, let's go'.

source.title: Mosaic Adventure: Glossary for Everest Base Camp Trek

versions.note: Bistarai, bistarai: slowly, slowly; jam jam: let's go, what the guide says when it's time to start moving.

source.title: Best Heritage Tour: Basic Nepali Words for Travelers

facts.claim: For a climbing Sherpa, guiding is the family's living and a duty: the season's pay keeps the family and the children at school, and sons follow their fathers onto the mountain.

versions.note: 'Taking clients to the summit is my duty.' He followed his father, who worked on Everest as a sirdar, the head Sherpa.

source.title: Anadolu: Nepali mountaineer Kami Rita Sherpa summits Everest for record 32nd time (2026)

versions.note: After the 2015 earthquake many spent most of the money they had saved for their children's education on rebuilding their homes.

source.title: National Geographic: Nepalis Hold Their Breath as New Everest Climbing Season Begins (2016)
